artworks.title: Psamathe
artworks.description: Oil on canvas, 85 × 66.5 cm, in the Lady Lever Art Gallery, Port Sunlight. Leighton's late academic-classical study presents the Nereid Psamathe alone on a sandy shore, her filmy drapery slipped from her shoulders onto the sand, arms folded about her drawn-up knees as she gazes out across a luminous Aegean. Turning the sea-nymph's back to the viewer, the painter distills her into a meditation on solitude and the tide, evoking the goddess of sandy beaches whom Aeacus once seized on this very kind of strand to father Phocus.

artworks.title: Psamathe fleeing among the Nereids (detail of the seizure of Thetis by Peleus)
artworks.description: Detail from an Attic red-figure vase of the Classical period, attributed to the Achilles Painter. The larger composition shows Peleus wrestling and seizing the sea-goddess Thetis; among the sister Nereids fleeing the struggle is Psamathe, here identified by inscription. The scene resonates with her own myth, for Psamathe was likewise captured on the shore by Peleus's father Aeacus — escaping into the form of a seal before he overpowered her and she bore him Phocus, whose name means 'seal.' Such named appearances in 5th-century BC Attic pottery are the principal ancient depictions of the Nereid.
